mainTopic: The days for weddings: why not on מוצאי שבת, when a בתולה and an אלמנה complete their marriage, and אגדות of בר קפרא.
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why a בתולה is not married on מוצאי שבת. The first reason, that people would do wedding calculations on שבת, is rejected: אביי shows from many sources that planning for a מצוה is allowed on שבת. רבי זירא gives a new reason. It is a גזירה, so that a busy host does not slaughter a bird on שבת for the feast. The same reason is then applied to ערב שבת. Next the גמרא asks whether a בתולה married on Wednesday waits until the night that begins Thursday, in case the groom's anger cools before court. בר קפרא's ברייתא shows the timing comes from the ברכה of creation, and the גמרא gives two reasons why an אלמנה waits until Friday. The amud closes with אגדות of בר קפרא: the work of צדיקים is greater than creating heaven and earth, and a פסוק about a 'peg' is read as a lesson about guarding one's ear. That lesson continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The reason: because of calculations
steps.stepSummary: The answer to why a בתולה is not married on מוצאי שבת: because of calculations.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because of calculations.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes an answer that began just before this section. We don't marry a בתולה on מוצאי שבת because the planning would lead people to do calculations on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wedding right after שבת means the planning, including counting costs and arranging the meal, would happen on שבת itself. That kind of weekday business is improper on שבת. This reason is about to be challenged.

phrases.english: Because of calculations.
phrases.notes: This answers the question just before: why don't we marry a בתולה right after שבת?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the question asked just before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No wedding on מוצאי שבת, so that people don't do wedding calculations on שבת.

steps.title: אביי: calculations for a מצוה are permitted
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges the reason: רב חסדא and רב המנונא say calculations for a מצוה are allowed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Are calculations for a מצוה forbidden? Don't רב חסדא and רב המנונא both say that calculations for a מצוה may be done on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the reason of חשבונות. A wedding is a מצוה, and calculations for a מצוה are allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason only works if all calculations are forbidden on שבת. רב חסדא and רב המנונא say that calculations for a מצוה are permitted. Wedding planning is for a מצוה, so it should be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Calculations done for the sake of a מצוה
But isn't it so that... (brings a challenge)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And are calculations for a מצוה forbidden?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב הַמְנוּנָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: But it was Rav Chisda and Rav Hamnuna who both said:

phrases.aramaic: חֶשְׁבּוֹנוֹת שֶׁל מִצְוָה מוּתָּר לְחַשְּׁבָן בְּשַׁבָּת!
phrases.english: Calculations for a מצוה may be reckoned on Shabbat!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְחֶשְׁבּוֹנוֹת שֶׁל מִצְוָה מִי אֲסִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that weddings on מוצאי שבת are banned because of calculations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calculations for a מצוה are allowed on שבת, and a wedding is a מצוה, so that cannot be the reason.

steps.title: More sources: charity, community needs, saving life
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds more sources: allocating צדקה, attending to community needs, and arranging פיקוח נפש are all allowed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: We may allocate צדקה to the poor on שבת. And רבי יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן: We may go to synagogues and study halls on שבת to take care of community matters. And רבי יעקב בר אידי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: We may take care of פיקוח נפש matters on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי keeps building his challenge with more examples. Each one shows that planning and arranging for a מצוה is allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are all kinds of מצוה business: deciding how much צדקה to give, handling community needs, and arranging to save a life. All are allowed on שבת, so wedding planning, which is also מצוה business, should be allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: To oversee, to take care of

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
One may allocate charity to the poor on Shabbat!

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yaakov said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
One may go to synagogues and study halls
to take care of community matters on Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
One may take care of saving a life on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: He means making the plans and arrangements to save someone, which also counts as מצוה business.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: פּוֹסְקִין צְדָקָה לַעֲנִיִּים בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more sources to support אביי's challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That arranging matters for a מצוה is allowed on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר, and two teachings of רבי יוחנן

steps.title: Even arranging a match is allowed on שבת
steps.stepSummary: Last sources: going to public arenas for community needs, and, from דבי מנשיא, arranging a match for a girl or schooling for a boy on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: We may go to theaters and circuses on שבת to take care of community matters. And it was taught in the school of מנשיא: We may arrange a match for a young girl to be betrothed on שבת, and arrange for a young boy to learn תורה and to learn a trade.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his list. The strongest source is the last one: arranging a שידוך is allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source from דבי מנשיא is very close to our case, since it deals with arranging a marriage. If even that planning is allowed on שבת, then wedding calculations cannot be the reason to avoid a wedding on מוצאי שבת. The reason of חשבונות is now pushed aside.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the school of מנשיא

steps.whatToRemember: All of these sources show that planning for a מצוה is allowed on שבת, so the reason of חשבונות falls away.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: And Rav Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan:
One may go to theaters and circuses
phrases.notes: These were public places of the non-Jews, where decisions affecting Jews were often made.

phrases.english: to take care of community matters on Shabbat.
And the school of Menashya taught:
One may arrange a match for a young girl to be betrothed on Shabbat,
and for a young boy, to have him taught Torah
and to have him taught a trade.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתָנָא דְּבֵי מְנַשְּׁיָא: מְשַׁדְּכִין עַל הַתִּינוֹקֶת לֵיאָרֵס בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's list of sources against the reason of חשבונות.
steps.raayaObject: That arranging a marriage, and other מצוה planning, is allowed on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יונתן, and the teaching of דבי מנשיא

steps.title: New reason: a decree lest one slaughter a bird
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא gives a new reason: a גזירה, so that the busy groom won't slaughter a young bird on שבת for the feast.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי זירא said: It is a גזירה, so that a person won't slaughter a young bird on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first reason was rejected, רבי זירא offers a different reason for not marrying on מוצאי שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is no longer about calculating. It is about doing a real מלאכה, slaughtering an animal. A groom rushing to prepare the feast for that night might forget it is שבת and slaughter a bird, so the חכמים made a גזירה against weddings on מוצאי שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer and gives a new one)
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Zeira said:
It is a decree, lest one slaughter a young bird.
phrases.notes: He means slaughtering it on שבת for the wedding feast that night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יִשְׁחוֹט בֶּן עוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason of חשבונות with a new reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban was because of calculations on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban is a גזירה so that no one slaughters a bird on שבת for the feast.

steps.title: אביי: then יום הכפורים on Monday should be moved
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges: by that logic, יום הכפורים should never fall on Monday, since one might slaughter a bird on שבת for the meal of ערב יום הכפורים on Sunday.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, then יום הכפורים that falls on Monday should be pushed off, because of a גזירה that a person might slaughter a young bird on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tests רבי זירא's reason on a similar case. If the fear of slaughtering on שבת is enough to ban weddings, it should also stop יום הכפורים from falling on Monday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יום הכפורים is on Monday, ערב יום הכפורים is Sunday, and eating a festive meal then is a מצוה. A person might slaughter a bird on שבת to prepare for it. Yet the calendar does not avoid this, so why worry about it for a wedding?

keyTerms.meaning: If so, then... (pushes a reason to an unwanted result)
Monday (the second day of the week)

steps.confusionAlert: בשני בשבת does not mean 'on שבת'. It means Monday, the second day of the week.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: If so,

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשֵׁנִי בְּשַׁבָּת יִדָּחֶה,
phrases.english: Yom Kippur that falls on Monday should be pushed off,
phrases.notes: He means the calendar should be set so that יום הכפורים never lands on Monday.

phrases.english: as a decree, lest one slaughter a young bird!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's new reason by comparing it to another case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's גזירה about slaughtering a bird.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same worry exists for the meal of ערב יום הכפורים on Sunday, yet we don't avoid having יום הכפורים on Monday.

steps.title: First answer: cooking for others makes one rushed
steps.stepSummary: Difference: for ערב יום הכפורים a person prepares for himself and is calm, but for a wedding he prepares for others and is under pressure.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, where it is for himself, he is not rushed. Here, where it is for others, he is rushed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי by showing the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone preparing his own meal is relaxed and will remember it is שבת. Someone hosting a wedding feast for guests is stressed and busy, so he is more likely to forget and slaughter on שבת. The גזירה is needed only where the pressure is real.

phrases.english: There, where it is for himself, he is not preoccupied,
phrases.notes: 'There' is ערב יום הכפורים; 'here' is the wedding.

phrases.english: here, where it is for others, he is preoccupied.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by distinguishing the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases carry the same risk of slaughtering on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wedding host is rushed because he cooks for others, so only there is a גזירה needed.

steps.title: Second answer: ערב יום הכפורים leaves time
steps.stepSummary: Another difference: for ערב יום הכפורים there is time on Sunday to slaughter, but a wedding feast on מוצאי שבת leaves no time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: there, he has extra time. Here, he does not have extra time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different way to tell the two cases apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meal of ערב יום הכפורים is eaten on Sunday during the day, so he can slaughter on Sunday after שבת ends. The wedding feast is right on מוצאי שבת, with no time after שבת, so he might be tempted to slaughter on שבת itself.
steps.whatToRemember: Final reason: no wedding on מוצאי שבת because of a גזירה about slaughtering on שבת. It is different from ערב יום הכפורים, either because the host is rushed for others or because there is no extra time.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: הָתָם אִית לֵיהּ רַוְוחָא,
phrases.english: Alternatively: there, he has extra time,
here, he does not have extra time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: הָתָם אִית לֵיהּ רַוְוחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to אביי's challenge, different from step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases carry the same risk of slaughtering on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: ערב יום הכפורים leaves time on Sunday to slaughter, while the wedding feast leaves none.

steps.title: The same decree explains the rule about ערב שבת
steps.stepSummary: Now that רבי זירא's reason has been accepted, the גמרא says the restriction on ערב שבת is also explained by the גזירה that the groom might slaughter a bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have reached this explanation, ערב שבת too is a גזירה, in case he slaughters a young bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the reason it just built up for מוצאי שבת and applies it to the case of ערב שבת as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5 through 8 set up the idea that a busy groom might slaughter a bird on שבת for the feast. Once that reason is in place, it also explains why a wedding is not held on ערב שבת. The rule is a protective גזירה, not a problem with the wedding act itself on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have come to this (explanation)

steps.whatToRemember: Both ערב שבת and מוצאי שבת weddings are avoided because of one worry: the groom might slaughter a bird on שבת for the feast.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
phrases.notes: "This" means רבי זירא's reason from step 5, the worry about slaughtering a bird.

phrases.english: ערב שבת too
is a decree, lest he slaughter a young bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the reason that steps 5 through 8 defended to a second case, ערב שבת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The restriction on ערב שבת is also a גזירה, in case the groom slaughters a young bird on שבת.

steps.title: Relations on Wednesday itself, or on the night beginning Thursday?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a בתולה married on Wednesday begins married life that night, or waits until Thursday because of a worry that the groom's anger might cool.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is a בתולה married on Wednesday and her marriage completed on Wednesday, so that we do not worry his anger will cool? Or perhaps she is married on Wednesday and her marriage completed on Thursday, because we do worry his anger will cool?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about timing, starting a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the groom has a virginity complaint, he should go to court while he is still upset. The question is whether we worry that a delay would let his anger cool. If we do worry, the marriage is completed only once Thursday begins, on the night that starts Thursday, so he can go straight to court that Thursday morning.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them
A woman marrying for the first time

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
Is a virgin married on Wednesday
and does she have relations on Wednesday,
and we are not concerned that his mind will cool,
phrases.notes: He means that if the groom has a virginity complaint, waiting a day might calm him down so he never goes to court.

phrases.english: or perhaps:
a virgin is married on Wednesday
and has relations on Thursday,
because we are concerned that his mind will cool.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the שבת discussion closes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do we worry that the groom's anger might cool, which would require completing the marriage on Thursday night instead of Wednesday?

steps.title: בר קפרא: the timing follows the ברכה of creation
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of בר קפרא says a בתולה waits until Thursday and an אלמנה until Friday because of the ברכה given on those days. This shows the cooling worry is not the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for בר קפרא taught: A בתולה is married on Wednesday and her marriage completed on Thursday, since the ברכה to the fish was said on that day. An אלמנה is married on Thursday and her marriage completed on Friday, since the ברכה to man was said on that day. So the reason is the ברכה, but we are not concerned about his anger cooling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question, then draws an inference from the reason the ברייתא gives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר קפרא agrees that a בתולה waits until Thursday, but his reason is the ברכה of 'פרו ורבו' given to the fish on day five. Since he gives that reason, the גמרא infers that the cooling worry is not a factor. This answers the question in step 10: we are not concerned about it.

keyTerms.meaning: Blessing (here, the blessing to be fruitful)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that in practice a בתולה still waits until Thursday. What changes is only the reason: the ברכה, not the worry about his anger cooling.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for בר קפרא taught:
A virgin is married on Wednesday
and has relations on Thursday,
since on it the blessing was said to the fish.
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:22

phrases.english: A widow is married on Thursday
and has relations on Friday
since on it the blessing was said to man.
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:28

phrases.english: So the reason is because of the blessing,
but about his mind cooling
we are not concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That we are not concerned about the groom's anger cooling.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of בר קפרא, which explains the days by the ברכה of creation rather than by the cooling worry.

steps.title: Why shouldn't a widow also use Thursday?
steps.stepSummary: If the ברכה decides the day, then an אלמנה married on Thursday should complete her marriage that same Thursday, the day of the fish's ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, an אלמנה too should have her marriage completed on Thursday, since the ברכה to the fish was said on that day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בר קפרא's rule for the אלמנה using his own reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thursday also has a ברכה, the one given to the fish. So why make the אלמנה wait until Friday? It seems she could complete her marriage on the same day she marries.

phrases.english: If so,
a widow too should have relations on Thursday,
since the blessing to the fish was said on it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions part of the ברייתא brought as proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר קפרא's ruling that an אלמנה waits until Friday.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברכה is what matters, Thursday already has the fish's ברכה, so there is no need to wait.

steps.title: Man's ברכה is better
steps.stepSummary: Since the אלמנה can reach the day of man's ברכה, that ברכה is preferable for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברכה of man is preferable to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in a few words: Friday's ברכה is better than Thursday's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both days carry a ברכה, but the ברכה given to man fits a person better than the one given to fish. Since the אלמנה can wait one day and reach man's ברכה, she does.
steps.whatToRemember: A בתולה completes her marriage on Thursday (the fish's ברכה) and an אלמנה on Friday (man's ברכה). The reason is the ברכה, not a worry that the groom's anger will cool.

phrases.english: The blessing of man is preferable to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ranking: one ברכה is better than the other.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any ברכה day is good enough, so an אלמנה should use Thursday.
steps.terutzMaskana: When man's ברכה is within reach, it is preferred, so an אלמנה waits for Friday.

steps.title: Another reason: the חכמים wanted the groom to rejoice for three days
steps.stepSummary: Instead of the ברכה, the reason for Friday may be that the חכמים wanted a man who marries an אלמנה to stay home and rejoice with her on Thursday, Friday, and שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, the reason is that the חכמים were diligent. As a ברייתא teaches: Why did they say that an אלמנה marries on Thursday and completes the marriage on Friday? Because if she completed it on Thursday, the next morning he would get up early and go off to his work. The חכמים were diligent to look after the good of Jewish women, so that he would rejoice with her for three days: Thursday, Friday, and שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to why an אלמנה waits until Friday. It brings a ברייתא that says the חכמים set this up so the groom would not leave her and go to work the next day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13 the reason was the ברכה given to man on Friday. Here the reason is practical: a groom who marries an אלמנה has no seven days of celebration, so he might rush back to work. If the marriage is completed on Friday, then Friday and שבת keep him home with her, so he rejoices with her for three days.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; or else (introduces another possible reason)
They were diligent; they took special care
The good and protection of Jewish women
A craft or trade; a person's work
Completes the marriage through living together as husband and wife

phrases.english: Alternatively: because they were diligent.
phrases.notes: "They" means the חכמים. This is another reason why an אלמנה waits until Friday.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: Why did they say
that a widow is married on Thursday
and completes the marriage on Friday?
Because if you say she should complete it on Thursday,
the next day he gets up early for his work and goes off.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁקְדוּ חֲכָמִים עַל תַּקָּנַת בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: The Sages were diligent about the good of Jewish women,
so that he should rejoice with her for three days:
Thursday, Friday, and Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reason for the same rule explained in step 13 by the ברכה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative reason for the same rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only reason for Friday is the ברכה given to man on that day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule could also be based on the חכמים' care that the groom stay home and rejoice with his wife for three days.

steps.title: What difference is there between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what case the reason of the ברכה and the reason of the חכמים' diligence would lead to a different result.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between the reason of the 'blessing' and the reason of 'they were diligent'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now has two reasons for the same rule, and it asks when it would actually matter which reason is the true one. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually both reasons give the same result: the marriage is completed on Friday. The גמרא wants a case where one reason applies and the other does not, so the two reasons are really different.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference is there between...? (asks for a practical difference)

phrases.english: What difference is there between "blessing" and "they were diligent"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the new reason from step 14 with the ברכה reason from step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two reasons would lead to a different practical outcome.

steps.title: Two cases where the reasons differ: a man without work, and יום טוב on Friday
steps.stepSummary: The difference shows up with a man who has no job, or when יום טוב falls on Friday. In those cases the groom will not go to work anyway, so only the ברכה reason still applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a man who is idle. Or else: a יום טוב that falls on Friday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two reasons differ when the groom would not go to work the next day anyway. It gives two such cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man who has no job will not leave his wife early in the morning to go to work. When יום טוב falls on Friday, he cannot work that day. In both cases the worry behind 'they were diligent' does not apply, but the ברכה of Friday still does.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
An idle person; a man who has no job
A festival day on which work is forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons why an אלמנה completes her marriage on Friday: the ברכה given to man, and the חכמים' care that he rejoice with her. They differ only when he would not go to work anyway.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: an idle man.
phrases.notes: He has no job, so he won't run off to work anyway. Only the 'blessing' reason is left.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: Or else: a Festival that falls on Friday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The reasons differ for an idle man and for יום טוב on Friday. In those cases the work worry does not apply, but the ברכה reason does.

steps.title: בר קפרא: the work of צדיקים is greater than creating heaven and earth
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא teaches that heaven and earth are described as made with one 'hand,' but the מקדש, which צדיקים built, is described as made with 'hands' in the plural.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא taught: The work of the righteous is greater than the making of heaven and earth. About heaven and earth it is written: 'My hand also founded the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens.' But about the work of the righteous it is written: 'The place You made for Yourself to dwell in, ה׳, the מקדש, my Lord, which Your hands established.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic: an אגדה taught by בר קפרא. It compares two פסוקים to show that the work of צדיקים is greater than the creation of the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about creation speaks of 'My hand,' in the singular. The פסוק about the מקדש, which was built by people, says 'Your hands,' in the plural. בר קפרא reads the plural as showing that the work of צדיקים is greater.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught or explained, usually by reading meaning into פסוקים
The creation of heaven and earth

steps.confusionAlert: The whole proof depends on one small detail: whether the word for 'hand' is singular or plural. Keep that in mind, because the next steps argue about exactly this point.

phrases.english: Bar Kappara taught:
Greater is the work of the righteous
than the making of heaven and earth,
for about the making of heaven and earth it is written:
"My hand also founded the earth
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 48:13. Notice that "hand" is singular here.

phrases.english: and My right hand spread out the heavens,"

phrases.aramaic: וְאִלּוּ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יְדֵיהֶם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים כְּתִיב:
phrases.english: whereas about the handiwork of the righteous it is written:
"The place for You to dwell in, which You made, ה׳,
phrases.notes: שמות 15:17. This is about the מקדש, which people built.

phrases.english: the Sanctuary, my Lord, which Your hands established."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: another teaching of בר קפרא, who was also quoted in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The work of צדיקים (the מקדש, described with 'hands') is greater than the creation of heaven and earth (described with 'hand').

steps.title: רבי חייא: a פסוק about creation also says 'His hands'
steps.stepSummary: A Babylonian named רבי חייא challenges בר קפרא from a פסוק about creation that seems to use the plural 'hands.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain Babylonian, whose name was רבי חייא, objected: But it says, 'And the dry land His hands formed'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא challenges בר קפרא's proof. He points to a פסוק about creation that also speaks of 'hands.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר קפרא's proof depends on creation being described with only one hand. If a פסוק about creating the dry land says 'His hands,' then creation is also described with the plural, and the proof falls apart.

phrases.english: A certain Babylonian responded,
and Rabbi Ḥiyya was his name:
"And the dry land His hands formed"!
phrases.notes: תהלים 95:5

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵשִׁיב בַּבְלִי אֶחָד, וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא שְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר קפרא's claim that creation is described only with one hand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק about creating the dry land uses 'His hands' in the plural, so creation is not described only in the singular.

steps.title: The word is spelled 'His hand'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that although the word is read 'His hands,' it is written 'His hand,' in the singular.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'His hand' is what is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends בר קפרא by looking at how the word is spelled in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is read as 'his hands' (יָדָיו), but it is spelled without the letter י, as 'his hand' (ידו). So the written text still speaks of one hand, and בר קפרא's proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written (how the word is spelled in the text)

phrases.english: "His hand" is written.
phrases.notes: We read it as 'His hands,' but it is spelled without a י, so it looks like 'His hand.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי חייא's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק says 'His hands,' in the plural.

steps.title: But the verb 'formed' is plural
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that even if 'hand' is spelled in the singular, the verb 'they formed' is plural.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it says 'formed' in the plural!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the last answer. The verb in the פסוק is plural, which suggests more than one hand did the forming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spelling 'His hand' solved the noun, but the verb יָצָרוּ means 'they formed.' A plural verb seems to show that the subject is plural after all.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written...? (introduces a challenge from the text)

phrases.english: But it is written "formed"!
phrases.notes: The verb means 'they formed,' which is plural.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the פסוק speaks of only one hand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verb 'formed' is plural, so it points to more than one hand.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the plural refers to God's fingers
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the plural verb refers to God's fingers, as another פסוק describes the heavens as the work of His fingers. So creation was still done with one hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: His fingers formed it, as it is written: 'When I see Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and stars which You established.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the last challenge. The plural verb refers to God's fingers, not to two hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק in תהלים calls the heavens 'the work of Your fingers.' So the plural 'formed' can mean that the fingers of one hand did the forming. Creation is still described with one hand, and בר קפרא's teaching stands.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (brings a supporting פסוק)
You established; You set in place

steps.whatToRemember: בר קפרא's teaching stands: creation is described with one hand (its fingers), while the מקדש, built by צדיקים, is described with 'hands.'

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
His fingers formed it,
as it is written: "When I see Your heavens,
phrases.notes: תהלים 8:4

phrases.english: the work of Your fingers,
the moon and stars which You established."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: יָצְרוּ אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 and closes the defense of בר קפרא's teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural verb means more than one hand formed the dry land.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural refers to the fingers of one hand, as the heavens are called 'the work of Your fingers.'

steps.title: A verse says the sky tells of the work of God's hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges בר קפרא with a פסוק that seems to describe the heavens as the work of God's 'hands,' in the plural.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: 'The heavens declare the glory of God, and the sky tells of the work of His hands!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new פסוק to attack בר קפרא's claim that heaven and earth were made with only one hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word 'His hands' (יָדָיו) is plural, and it seems to be talking about the sky that God made. The earlier answers about spelling and fingers do not easily work here, so the challenge looks strong again.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"The heavens declare the glory of God,
phrases.notes: תהלים 19:2

phrases.english: and the sky tells of the work of His hands!"
phrases.notes: The point of the challenge is 'His hands,' in the plural, which seems to describe how the sky was made.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the fingers answer saved בר קפרא, a new פסוק is brought against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר קפרא's claim that heaven and earth were made with one hand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק uses the plural 'His hands' in connection with the sky, which suggests creation was done with two hands.

steps.title: The sky reveals the work of the righteous through rain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the פסוק: the sky tells of the work of the צדיקים, and it does this by bringing rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the verse means: who tells of the work of the hands of the righteous? The sky. And how does it do that? Through rain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining that the 'hands' in the פסוק are not God's hands at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads 'the work of His hands' as the deeds of the צדיקים. The sky shows that their deeds are good by sending rain. So the פסוק is not describing how the sky was made, and בר קפרא's one-hand teaching still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a rereading of the source)

steps.whatToRemember: Every challenge to בר קפרא is answered. Creation was done with God's one 'hand,' while the מקדש was built with 'hands,' through the צדיקים.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
The work of the hands of the righteous,
who tells of it? The sky.
And what is that? Rain.
phrases.notes: When rain falls because of the צדיקים' prayers, the sky is showing that their deeds are good.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 by rereading the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק so it is about a different subject
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'The work of His hands' means the sky that God made with His hands.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'His hands' refers to the deeds of the צדיקים, which the sky reveals through rain.

steps.title: A peg on your ear: guarding yourself from improper speech
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא rereads the פסוק about a 'peg' among your weapons as 'a peg on your ear.' It teaches what a person should do if he hears something improper.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא expounded: What does the verse mean, 'And you shall have a peg among your weapons'? Do not read 'your weapons,' but rather 'on your ear.' This teaches that if a person hears something improper...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching of בר קפרא. He rereads a word in a פסוק to learn a lesson about the ear, and the lesson continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק literally talks about a digging tool carried with a soldier's gear. By reading the same letters as אָזְנֶךָ, 'your ear,' בר קפרא turns it into a lesson about protecting your ears. The end of the sentence, what the person should do, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounded, taught a deeper meaning of a פסוק
Do not read it as ... but rather as (a reading with different vowels)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not change the written פסוק or its plain meaning. It reads the same letters with different vowels to teach an extra lesson.

phrases.english: Bar Kappara expounded:
What is meant by that which is written:
"And you shall have a peg among your weapons"?
phrases.notes: דברים 23:14

phrases.english: Do not read it as "your weapons,"
but rather as "on your ear,"
phrases.notes: Same letters, just read with different vowels.

phrases.english: meaning that if a person hears
something improper,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new aggadic teaching from the same חכם, בר קפרא, after his earlier teaching was defended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'peg' of the פסוק is read as being 'on your ear.' It teaches a person how to respond when he hears improper words (the full lesson continues next).
